::: {.lead}
Today you work like a team at the office. Each experiment has two parts.
**Part A** is in the apps of your university account: e-mail (Outlook), the
calendar and Word. **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson:
on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step,
write your result in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the
table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer and your university account (Outlook on the
  web at `outlook.office.com`, or the Outlook app; Word).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer or in the Outlook app on your phone.
- **Send only to your own address** in Part A. Nobody else gets a test
  e-mail or a test meeting.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · A clear e-mail with a file

**The idea:** an e-mail has **To** (the people who must read it and act),
**Cc** (the people who only need to know), a **subject** (what it is about,
in a few words), the message, and an **attachment** (a file, with the
paperclip). **Reply** answers only the sender. **Reply all** answers
everyone in To and Cc. **Forward** sends the e-mail and its file to a new
person.

**Aim:** send a clear e-mail with the right file, and choose Reply, Reply
all or Forward.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Outlook)**
:::

1. Click **New mail**. To: your own address. Subject: `Agenda: staff
   meeting on Sunday`. **Attach** (the paperclip) `agenda-start.docx` and
   click **Send**. Find the e-mail in your Inbox.

   {{< record "In the Inbox, the sign of a file is" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A **paperclip** next to the e-mail. When you open it, the file
   `agenda-start.docx` is under the subject. A clear subject says what the
   e-mail is about before anybody opens it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which sign in the Inbox shows that an e-mail has a file?

   - [x] a paperclip

     Why: The paperclip is the sign of an attachment.

   - [ ] a flag

     Why: A flag marks an e-mail to do later.

   - [ ] a red exclamation mark

     Why: It marks an e-mail of high importance, with or without a file.
   :::

2. Open the e-mail. Click **Reply**: is the file there? Close it. Then
   click **Forward** and look again.

   {{< record "With Reply the file is … ; with Forward the file is …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   With **Reply** the file is **not there**: a reply goes back to the
   sender, who has the file. With **Forward** the file **is there**:
   Forward sends the e-mail and its file to a new person. The subject
   starts with **RE:** for a reply and **FW:** for a forward.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Reply, Reply all or Forward? Sort them.

   Reply
   :   answers only the sender

       Why: Reply goes back to one person: the sender.

   Reply all
   :   answers the sender and everyone in To and Cc

       Why: Everyone in the e-mail sees the answer.

   Forward
   :   sends the e-mail to a new person

       Why: Forward is for people who were not in the e-mail.

   :   keeps the attachment

       Why: The new person does not have the file yet, so Forward keeps it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/mail-lab.html" poster="sims/mail-lab.png" title="Mail Lab: To, Cc, subject and file" >}}

3. In **Mail Lab**, do Tasks 1 to 5. Task 1: who is in To and in Cc?

   {{< record "Task 1: To … ; Cc …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **To:** Omar and Lina (they come to the meeting). **Cc:** Mr Yousef (he
   only needs to know). Sami is not in the e-mail: the meeting is not for
   him.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Task 1, Mr Yousef, the manager, only needs to know about the agenda.
   Where does he go?

   - [x] in Cc

     Why: Cc is for the people who only need to know.

   - [ ] in To

     Why: To is for the people who must read the e-mail and act.

   - [ ] in the subject

     Why: The subject says what the e-mail is about, not who reads it.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A meeting in the calendar, online

**The idea:** a **meeting invitation** is an event of the calendar that you
send to people: a title, the date, the start and end time, the
**attendees**, and a room or an **online meeting** link (Teams, Google Meet
or Zoom). Each attendee answers **Accept**, **Tentative** (maybe) or
**Decline**, and the meeting goes into their calendar. First find a time
when everybody is free. In an online meeting, turn off your microphone when
you do not speak.

**Aim:** invite people at a time when all of them are free, with an online
meeting link.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (the Outlook calendar)**
:::

1. In the **Calendar**, click **New event**: `Staff meeting`, next Sunday,
   10:00 to 10:30. Turn on **Teams meeting**. Invite your own address,
   click **Send**, and open the event.

   {{< record "The event has a link or a button to" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Join**: the online meeting link. At 10:00 each attendee clicks Join
   and takes part from any place, on a computer or a phone.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What does the online meeting link let the attendees do?

   - [x] join the meeting from any place, on a computer or a phone

     Why: The link opens the online meeting (Teams, Meet or Zoom).

   - [ ] open the agenda file

     Why: The agenda is an attachment or a shared file, not the meeting link.

   - [ ] change the time of the meeting

     Why: Only the organizer changes the time.
   :::

2. Open the invitation in your Inbox. Find its three answer buttons.

   {{< record "The three answers" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Accept**, **Tentative** and **Decline** (in Google Calendar: **Yes**,
   **Maybe** and **No**). The organizer sees every answer.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which answer does each attendee give? Sort them.

   Accept
   :   Omar will come.

       Why: Accept puts the meeting in his calendar.

   Tentative
   :   Lina may have a class at that time.

       Why: Tentative means maybe.

   Decline
   :   Sami is on holiday that day.

       Why: Decline tells the organizer that he cannot come.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/meeting-planner.html" poster="sims/meeting-planner.png" title="Meeting Planner: a time for everybody" >}}

3. In **Meeting Planner**, find Sunday's first free hour for all three,
   then Room 21 or Online.

   {{< record "First free hour: … ; Room 21 or Online: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **11:00 to 12:00**: Huda is busy from 8:00 to 9:00, Omar from 9:00 to
   10:00, and Lina from 10:00 to 11:00. **Online**, because Omar works from
   home on Sunday.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="11:00|11|11.00|11:00-12:00|11:00 to 12:00" hint="Look for the first hour with no busy block in all three rows."}
   Sunday: Huda is busy 8:00–9:00, Omar 9:00–10:00 and Lina 10:00–11:00.
   At what time does the first free hour start?

   Why: From 11:00 to 12:00 nobody is busy, so the meeting starts at 11:00.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · One file, edited together

**The idea:** do not send copies back and forth. Keep **one** file in
OneDrive and share it with **Can edit**: people change the same file at the
same time (**co-editing**), and AutoSave keeps every change. A **comment**
is a note next to the text (Review › New Comment); type **\@** and a name,
and that person gets an e-mail. **Version History** keeps the older
versions of the file, and you can restore one.

**Aim:** share one file to edit it together, add a comment, and find an
older version.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word, a file in OneDrive)**
:::

1. Save `agenda-start.docx` in **OneDrive** (File › Save As). Click
   **Share**: **Specific people**, **Can edit**. (Do not send it.)

   {{< record "Who: … ; what they can do: …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Specific people**, **Can edit**: only the colleagues of the meeting
   get the link, and they can add their points to the agenda.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Omar and Lina must add their points to the agenda. Which settings?

   - [x] Specific people, Can edit

     Why: Only the two of them get the link, and they can change the file.

   - [ ] Anyone with the link, Can edit

     Why: The link can travel to strangers, and they could change the agenda.

   - [ ] Specific people, Can view

     Why: With Can view they can read the agenda, but not add their points.
   :::

2. Select **10:00**. Click **Review › New Comment**, type `Is 10:00 OK?`
   and **Post**. Then click **File › Info › Version History**.

   {{< record "The comment is on the … side; the older versions are in" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The comment is on the **right** side, next to the text. **Version
   History** lists the older versions with their date and time; open one
   and click **Restore** to bring it back.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Huda deleted a line of the agenda by mistake. Put the steps to bring it
   back in order.

   1. Click File › Info › Version History.
   2. Choose the version from before the mistake.
   3. Open the version.
   4. Click Restore.

   Why: Version History keeps the older versions; Restore brings one back.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/share-settings.html" poster="sims/share-settings.png" title="Share Settings: who and what?" >}}

3. In **Share Settings**, do Tasks 1 to 4. Task 2: Sami must add two
   slides. Which settings?

   {{< record "Task 2: who … ; what …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Specific people** (Sami) and **Can edit**: only Sami gets the link,
   and he can add the slides.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Task 3, every customer who gets the link may read the price list.
   Which settings?

   - [x] Anyone with the link, Can view

     Why: The customers are not in the company, and they only read.

   - [ ] People in your organization, Can view

     Why: The customers are not in the organization, so the link would not open.

   - [ ] Anyone with the link, Can edit

     Why: Customers must not change the prices.
   :::
